_about: Turn constants for the simulation (scripts/sim/sim_rules.gd reads this). ALL PROPOSED by Track S, 2026-10-09: the design doc leaves turn length open (Game concept > Turn length and action counts: 'Still to decide: how long a turn is'). Every tunable is a value record: {value, _proposed, _reason} until a decision replaces _proposed with a decision id from data/decisions/decisions.json.

turn_seconds._reason: Steambirds resolves 'a couple of seconds' per turn; 5 s lets a fighter at cruise turn ~100 degrees per turn, so a full circle takes about four turns and a minute of flight is 12 turns

step_rule._reason: the design doc's own proposal (Turn length and action counts): a fixed span of simulated time, split into each unit type's actions_per_turn equal steps; step_dt = turn_seconds / actions_per_turn

map_bounds_m._reason: the smallest round square that holds the exit criterion's minute of flight with full turns for every air unit; arithmetic in _derivation. Origin top-left, x right, y down, metres, like the prototype's canvas

_derivation: Exit criterion 5 (Alex): 'a map big enough to fly the planes around for a minute and complete full turns without leaving it'. Read here (proposed) as one minute of SIMULATED flight at cruise speed.
Per air unit, from its data/units/<id>.json envelope: cruise radius r_c = v_cruise / turn_rate(v_cruise); top-speed radius r_max = v_max / turn_rate(v_max).

A minute at cruise is P = 60 s x v_cruise of path, flown as a racetrack lap: two half-turns at r_c (one full turn, 2 pi r_c) and two straights S = (P - 2 pi r_c) / 2. The lap's long side is S + 2 r_c.
Room to turn away from an edge met at full speed is one top-speed radius at each end, so the side must be at least S + 2 r_c + 2 r_max.

Worst case heavy_fighter, 4,793 m: rounded up to a 5,000 m square. scripts/tests/test_unit_defs.gd recomputes this from the unit files, so retuning a plane faster or less agile fails the gate until the map grows with it.

SCALE NOTE (an open question, not decided here): the design doc leaves pixels per world unit open (Open design details > Camera and scale). If the prototype's 38 px canopy is a ~10 m tree (about 3.8 px/m), this map is about 19,000 px across and a fighter at cruise moves about 1,900 px per turn.
